doc.title: James Moody — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Years in Canada
summary: He lived in Canada after a relationship there, found it an extension of America, and kept working on the road.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: We didn't really talk much about your years in Canada yesterday. What kinds of things you were doing. What kind of groups you were working with up there.

I was in Canada. I had a relationship with a person in Canada, and that relationship with the person in Canada owned a boutique shop up there. And it was one of those things where it was a good lesson for me, a good experience. Because see when you have different experiences like that, it makes you appreciate much more when you got a gem. You know. You know. I got a gem, boy. And I know what I have. Mainly because I was in another predicament before.
Was it difficult living out of the country for those three years? That was what? '85, '88.
Canda is like an extension of America.
Yeah. Yeah. It's an extension. Snow up to your eyeballs, you know, in the wintertime and warm in the summertime. You know, people are pleasant.

People are pleasant everywhere. It depends on you, like I said yesterday. You know. It depends on how people treat you by the way you are. And so it was all right. But most of all like I met some nice people up there. And like it was a good experience for me. And I'm glad it happened, because it like – I can really appreciate what I've got now. You know?
Were you working mostly with a small group up there?
No. No. I wasn't working in Canada. See, it doesn't make any difference where I live Lida. I still work on the road.
Ah, I see what you're saying. Okay.
So, I mean I was still traveling. I'd be in Europe, Japan. You know. So that's what that was.
